title: Snapchat no longer rewards fully AI-generated Spotlight content
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: Snapchat has adjusted its recommendation systems to ensure that only videos created by real people are eligible for Spotlight recommendations, taking a stance against AI slop.
body:
Snapchat is taking a definitive step to champion human creativity on its platform, announcing that fully AI-generated videos will no longer be eligible for recommendations within its popular Spotlight feature. This strategic shift aims to recalibrate Snapchat's recommendation systems, ensuring that only content genuinely crafted by individuals receives prime visibility. While the platform isn't outright banning AI—creators can still leverage its AI-powered tools for enhancing or editing their original content—the core message is clear: authentic, human-made storytelling will be prioritized for discovery.

This move by Snapchat underscores a significant industry-wide re-evaluation of AI-generated content, particularly in response to the proliferation of "AI slop." The company's commitment to rewarding "original perspectives, personal storytelling, and the moments that people choose to create and share themselves" signals a broader trend among social platforms to foster genuine engagement and quality over sheer volume. For developers and researchers, this highlights a critical evolving landscape: the value proposition of AI in content creation is shifting from pure generation to augmentation and enhancement, emphasizing the enduring importance of human input and creativity in a world increasingly saturated with AI-produced material. This trend, mirrored by initiatives from platforms like LinkedIn and Substack to identify or deprioritize AI-generated content, suggests a growing demand for tools that empower human creators rather than replace them entirely.
